title: Regeneration Verification + Final Catalog Accuracy Certification
premise: No catalog corrections were made in AQ-03A-C. Both findings this initiative was originally built to fix (cheese scientific_name, squash-family taxonomy) were retracted after reading governance — the catalog was already correct on both counts. The scientific-identity phase found one non-blocking data-completeness gap (marionberry) that was deliberately not auto-corrected (Rule 3). The canonical-identity phase surfaced 18 alias-usage candidates for future editorial review, also not auto-corrected. Rule 2's regeneration guarantee is therefore verified against a genuinely unchanged catalog layer, which is itself a meaningful thing to prove rather than an anticlimax.

catalog_diff.verification: git status confirmed zero changes to any data/*-catalog.json file throughout AQ-03A-C.

regeneration_verification.unintended_drift: None — rerunning certification against unchanged catalogs produced zero diffs in data/generated, data/pages, or any publication artifact.

success_criteria_assessment.no_known_systematic_scientific_name_misu: TRUE — 1,165/1,166 entities conform (99.91%); the 1 exception is a data-completeness gap on a single cultivar entity, not a systematic pattern, and not auto-corrected pending editorial sourcing.
success_criteria_assessment.no_known_systematic_taxonomy_drift: TRUE — 0 structural violations across 1,166 entities; the only two candidate 'drift' patterns identified by prior audits (cheese, squash) were confirmed to be intentional, documented governance, not drift.
success_criteria_assessment.no_unresolved_ownership_ambiguity: TRUE for structural ownership (0 dangling references, 0 duplicate IDs, 0 cross-domain intrinsic-data duplication detected). PARTIAL for alias-level naming: 34 raw alias collisions surfaced, correctly triaged into governed-and-expected (13), likely-correct-modeling-with-imprecise-field-usage (10), and genuine editorial candidates (8) — none confirmed as errors, all require domain-expert judgment this process should not substitute for.
success_criteria_assessment.governed_vocabulary: TRUE — every checked vocabulary (usage_intensity across 8 domains, cheese's 8 frozen fields, vegetable's substitute culinary_role/flavor_intensity fields) conforms 100% to governance-documented enums.
success_criteria_assessment.deterministic_regeneration: TRUE — reconfirmed across all 11 domains with zero drift.
success_criteria_assessment.zero_publication_regressions: TRUE — all 11 domains recertified PASS, 100% publication completeness, no changes required.

recommendation: The Food Ontology Suite's catalog layer can be treated as editorially authoritative on the two specific dimensions this initiative examined (scientific identity, taxonomy/classification) and on structural/vocabulary integrity suite-wide. It is not yet fully closed on canonical-identity precision: 8 variety-pair candidates (e.g. mandarin/clementine, cranberry-bean/borlotti-bean) and 10 processed-form alias-field-usage cases warrant a scoped editorial pass, not because they are confirmed errors but because this audit cannot responsibly resolve culinary/botanical judgment calls by assumption. Recommended next step: a governance-led review of reports/catalog-canonical-identity.json's bucket B and C findings, informed by domain expertise rather than further automated verification.
